title: van der Waals isotherms around the critical point
caption: In reduced units (p, V, T divided by their critical values) the van der Waals isotherms are p = 8T/(3V − 1) − 3/V². Above T_c (here T = 1.1) the curve is smooth; at T_c it has a flat inflection exactly at (1, 1), the critical point; below T_c (T = 0.9) it has a wiggle where liquid and gas coexist. For CO₂, T_c = 8a/(27Rb) = 304 K.
alt: Three reduced van der Waals isotherms: a smooth one above the critical temperature, one with a flat inflection at the point (1, 1), and one below with a dip and a hump.
description: Axes: reduced volume V/V_c and reduced pressure p/p_c.
T = 1.1 T_c: pressure falls monotonically with volume.
T = T_c: the curve is flat (gradient 0) as it passes through (1, 1): the critical point where liquid and gas become identical.
T = 0.9 T_c: the curve has a minimum and a maximum; the equal-area construction replaces that part by a horizontal line. CO₂: T_c = 8 × 0.364/(27 × 8.31 × 4.27 × 10⁻⁵) = 304 K.
